title: Atman and Brahman: What the Pair Means
h1: Atman and Brahman: What the Pair Means
excerpt: Atman is the self and brahman is ultimate reality. Advaita teaches their non-difference. Other schools do not.

quick_answer.question: What is the difference between atman and brahman?
quick_answer.answer: Atman means the self and brahman means ultimate reality. In Advaita Vedanta the deepest teaching says they are not two. Other Vedanta schools describe a real distinction or a qualified relation.

intro: English often translates both words toward soul or God and then asks how two souls differ. The Sanskrit pair is more precise, and the precision is the argument.

sections.heading: How is each word used?
sections.content:
Atman is the self that traditions urge people not to confuse with the changing body and personality. Brahman is the ultimate that the Upanishads gesture toward, not a character in a story. Putting the words side by side is already a Vedantic habit.

The neighboring page is [the atman glossary](/glossary/atman/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: What does Advaita add?
sections.content:
Advaita, outlined in the Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy, says ignorance superimposes difference. Knowledge is said to reveal non-difference. Theistic commentators argue that devotion and distinction are not a beginner error to be erased. Both are Vedanta.

A wider map lives at the [Vedanta topic](/topics/vedanta/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: Why do other schools resist?
sections.content:
Read the glossary entries, then one Upanishadic passage in a public translation, then notice which commentator you are being handed. A class that says you are brahman is teaching Advaita or a popular descendant. It is not teaching every school.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [the brahman glossary](/glossary/brahman/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Non-difference is not a license to ignore other people or your own limits. It is a metaphysical claim. This site does not report it as a scientific discovery about consciousness.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Atman is self. Brahman is ultimate reality.
Advaita identifies them at the deepest level.
The claim is doctrine, not a lab result.

faq.question: Is this the same as non-duality?
faq.answer: Non-duality is a wider English label. Advaita is one important source of that label, not the only tradition that gets filed under it.

faq.question: Which page is the overview?
faq.answer: Use the Vedanta explainer and the question on how teachers describe the self.
